questions.question: What does a plastic face shield protect the rider from?

options.text: Insects.
Headlight glare.
Noise.
Sunshine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and small rocks thrown from other vehicles.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Which one is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no obvious defects, such as cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: A good helmet should meet U.S. DOT and state standards, fit snugly around your head, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks does not affect its safety.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control a motorcycle on?

options.text: Wet pavement
A driveway
Dry pavement
A parking lot

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet pavement
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride slowly and carefully on these surfaces.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?

options.text: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
Wear dark clothing.
Ride without your headlight.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear brightly-colored clothing when riding. This makes you easier for other drivers to see.

questions.question: How often should you do a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Before every ride.
About once every 10 rides.
Once a month.
Once a season.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle can cause serious accidents. Check your motorcycle before each ride to stay safe.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you must cross a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: When should you keep more space between your motorcycle and the car ahead?

options.text: When conditions make stopping harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When conditions make stopping harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space when the road is slippery, you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy. Extra space gives you time to stop safely.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-ride inspection?

options.text: The wear and tread of your tires
The cushion on your seat
The shine of your paint
The wind direction

questions.correctAnswerText: The wear and tread of your tires
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to get away from them.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If a car is tailgating you, change lanes and let them pass if you can. Speeding up will not help. The driver will just tailgate you at a higher speed, making things more dangerous.

questions.question: Smoothly downshifting on motorcycles:

options.text: Does not help.
Can help slow the motorcycle using engine power.
Is against the law.
Should not be done near other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help slow the motorcycle using engine power.
questions.explanation: Engine braking by downshifting smoothly is useful for slowing down. If you use engine braking, press your brake light separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch out for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking spot.
Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
Cars coming toward you.
Loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. A car may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave its parking space.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: Easier to see than a car's brake lights.
Harder to see than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More visible than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to see than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as bright as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should always look ahead for:

options.text: Road problems.
Traffic problems.
Ways to escape danger.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead to watch for changing traffic, road hazards, and escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any danger.

questions.question: The most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a good helmet and fasten it tightly.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet and fasten it tightly.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened tightly is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not remove alcohol.

questions.question: When riding in traffic, remember that motorcycles:

options.text: Are too small to have blind spots.
Have blind spots too small to be a problem.
Have blind spots that need to be checked by looking back.
Have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots that need to be checked by looking back.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always look back over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend in with traffic and avoid being noticed.
Use turn signals only at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers see you. Signal your turns, use your brake light, and stay in the right lane position. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, look 12 seconds ahead, and be ready to respond to any danger.

questions.question: When about to pass another vehicle, ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: You can see farther ahead.
You cannot see as far ahead.
It is hard to see around the vehicle.
It lets the other driver go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you see farther and makes other drivers more likely to see you.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift to neutral first.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When shifting to a lower gear, shift down one gear at a time. Slowly release the clutch between each downshift.

questions.question: The faster you drink:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster alcohol leaves your body.
The less the alcohol will affect you.
The less likely you will be stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding on a bridge grating, you should:

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of the lane.
Always stay on the far left side of the lane.
Slowly zigzag across the grating.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is usually not dangerous. Stay relaxed and ride straight across at a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the weave, as this is more dangerous and forces you out of your lane.

questions.question: Common drugs, such as cold tablets:

options.text: Can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle.
Usually will not affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle.
Do not affect your riding ability at all.
Are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can affect your ability to safely ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Learn about the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which affects how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner, keep a larger space between you and other vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: For the best protection, jackets and pants:

options.text: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
Should be loose and flap in the wind while riding.
Should only cover part of your arms and legs.
Should be made of wool.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For good protection, jackets and pants should cover your arms and legs completely. They should fit snug but be loose enough to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials work best in an accident.
